examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Trace which sources can reach each ALU input through its multiplexers and where the result is captured. A datapath’s capability depends on these connections, not on an assumed ISA. Booth multiplication acts on adjacent multiplier-bit pairs, including the appended low zero; additions/subtractions correspond to transitions, while repeated bits use shifts only.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
For a four-bit Booth multiplier Q=0110 with appended Q−1=0, how many add/subtract operations occur?

**Answer: 2.** Neighbouring pairs from low to high are 00,10,11,01. Only 10 and 01 trigger subtraction/addition, so there are two operations. Arithmetic shifts still occur for each iteration.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
All register next values at a clock edge use old values. Do not update one datapath register and immediately use its new value in another simultaneous assignment.

Do not treat ALU flags as interchangeable: zero, carry and signed overflow express different conditions.
